sentences.en: Hi, I'm Andrew Ross-Sorkin.
sentences.zh: 你好，我是安德鲁·罗斯-索金。

sentences.en: I cover business and policy for DealBook, a daily newsletter at the New York Times.
sentences.zh: 我为《纽约时报》的每日通讯《DealBook》报道商业和政策新闻。

sentences.en: On November 18th, I'm going to be interviewing some of the most consequential leaders in business, politics, and culture, including J.D.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我将在纽约市举行的DealBook峰会上现场采访一些商业、政治和文化领域最具影响力的人物，包括J.D.

sentences.en: Vance, Elon Musk, Christine Lagarde, Zilran Mondani, and many others, live on stage at the DealBook Summit in New York City.
sentences.zh: 万斯、埃隆·马斯克、克里斯蒂娜·拉加德、齐尔兰·蒙达尼以及其他许多人。

sentences.en: You can watch some of these unguarded, unfiltered conversations as they happen.
sentences.zh: 你可以实时观看其中一些毫无防备、未经剪辑的对话。

sentences.en: We're going to be live-streaming select interviews for anyone to watch, free, at nytimes.com on November 18th.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我们将在nytimes.com上免费直播部分精选采访，供所有人观看。

sentences.en: If you're not already a subscriber, you can download the New York Times app to watch and get a month of free access to all of our journalism.
sentences.zh: 如果你还不是订阅者，可以下载《纽约时报》应用程序进行观看，并获得我们所有新闻内容一个月的免费访问权限。

sentences.en: I hope you'll tune in.
sentences.zh: 希望你能收看。

sentences.en: You won't want to miss it.
sentences.zh: 你一定不想错过。

sentences.en: Hey, it's Michael.
sentences.zh: 嘿，我是迈克尔。

sentences.en: This morning on The Daily, I mentioned that our guest, politics reporter Astead Herndon, is launching a show dedicated to the midterm elections.
sentences.zh: 今天早上在《The Daily》节目中，我提到我们的嘉宾、政治记者阿斯特德·赫恩登正在推出一档专门报道中期选举的节目。

sentences.en: That show, The Run-Up, will explore both the forces at play in this election, and how it is that we've arrived at such a fraught moment in our politics.
sentences.zh: 这档节目名为《The Run-Up》，将探讨这次选举中发挥作用的各种力量，以及我们是如何走到今天这个政治局势如此紧张的时刻的。

sentences.en: Take a listen to the first episode.
sentences.zh: 请听听第一集。

sentences.en: Hi, my name is Astead Herndon.
sentences.zh: 你好，我叫阿斯特德·赫恩登。

sentences.en: I'm a politics reporter at the New York Times and hosting a new politics podcast from the Times.
sentences.zh: 我是《纽约时报》的政治记者，正在主持一档来自《时报》的全新政治播客。

sentences.en: I'm looking for Belinda.
sentences.zh: 我在找贝琳达。

sentences.en: Is this her?
sentences.zh: 是她吗？

sentences.en: Thank you for picking up.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你接电话。

sentences.en: We were hoping that you had maybe five, ten minutes today for us to ask a few questions about how you're feeling about politics right now, and then record that.
sentences.zh: 我们想看看你今天是否能抽出五到十分钟，让我们问几个关于你目前对政治感受的问题，并将其录制下来。

sentences.en: Is that something you think we could do right now?
sentences.zh: 你觉得我们现在可以这样做吗？

sentences.en: How long have you been a reporter at the New York Times?
sentences.zh: 你在《纽约时报》当记者多久了？

sentences.en: Since 2018.
sentences.zh: 从2018年开始。

sentences.en: I worked at the Boston Globe before that.
sentences.zh: 在那之前我在《波士顿环球报》工作。

sentences.en: And what area are you in?
sentences.zh: 你负责哪个领域？

sentences.en: I write about politics.
sentences.zh: 我写政治报道。

sentences.en: So I was on the election trail last cycle covering the presidential election.
sentences.zh: 上一轮选举周期我一直在竞选一线报道总统大选。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: And we're played later, or what?
sentences.zh: 我们是晚点再聊，还是怎么着？

sentences.en: Yeah, no problem.
sentences.zh: 好的，没问题。

sentences.en: We are talking to a lot of different types of voters so that some of our listeners get a sense of how people across the country are feeling.
sentences.zh: 我们正在采访各种不同类型的选民，以便让我们的听众了解全国各地人们的感受。

sentences.en: Okay, we can try it.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我们可以试试。

sentences.en: I don't read the Times.
sentences.zh: 我不看《时报》。

sentences.en: It's way too liberal for me.
sentences.zh: 对我来说它太自由派了。

sentences.en: I'm not expecting a whole lot from this conversation, but I'll give it a shot, okay?
sentences.zh: 我对这次谈话没抱太大期望，但我会试一试，好吗？

sentences.en: Uh, we are in Beaverdale, Iowa.
sentences.zh: 呃，我们在爱荷华州的比弗代尔。

sentences.en: Uh, we're in Charleston, South Carolina.
sentences.zh: 呃，我们在南卡罗来纳州的查尔斯顿。

sentences.en: What direction are we?
sentences.zh: 我们是什么方向？

sentences.en: West?
sentences.zh: 西边？

sentences.en: Headed to this church, but late.
sentences.zh: 正赶往教堂，但迟到了。

sentences.en: As a pastor's son, I know that is a cardinal sin.
sentences.zh: 作为牧师的儿子，我知道这是弥天大罪。

sentences.en: As I've been preparing to cover the 2022 midterms, I keep thinking back to a few years ago.
sentences.zh: 在准备报道2022年中期选举时，我不断回想起几年前。

sentences.en: I'm walking up to this house.
sentences.zh: 我正走向这所房子。

sentences.en: When I was out in the field covering the presidential election.
sentences.zh: 当时我正在一线报道总统大选。

sentences.en: We see some Trump signs.
sentences.zh: 我们看到了一些特朗普的标语。

sentences.en: It was Donald Trump's America.
sentences.zh: 那是唐纳德·特朗普的美国。

sentences.en: More Trump signs.
sentences.zh: 还有更多的特朗普标语。

sentences.en: And Joe Biden's whole campaign was built around getting Trump out of office and unifying the country.
sentences.zh: 而乔·拜登的整个竞选活动都是围绕着让特朗普下台并统一国家展开的。

sentences.en: He said he wanted to restore the soul of the nation.
sentences.zh: 他说他想恢复国家的灵魂。

sentences.en: Do you think that Biden becoming president will lead to more unity in the country?
sentences.zh: 你认为拜登当选总统会使国家更加团结吗？

sentences.en: I'm not optimistic about that.
sentences.zh: 我不对此感到乐观。

sentences.en: You can't force people into unity.
sentences.zh: 你无法强迫人们团结。

sentences.en: First of all, all this talk about unity and healing and stuff.
sentences.zh: 首先，所有关于团结、治愈之类的言论。

sentences.en: But the question.
sentences.zh: 但问题是。

sentences.en: You know, we're not unifying and healing with these guys.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们和这些人是无法实现团结和治愈的。

sentences.en: Was whether that was even possible.
sentences.zh: 这是否真的可能。

sentences.en: When I hear, like, those calls from Biden for unity, I'm thinking, like, okay, but what are the steps for justice that need to happen before we can get there?
sentences.zh: 当我听到拜登呼吁团结时，我在想，好吧，但在我们实现目标之前，需要采取哪些正义的步骤？

sentences.en: Let's have some consequences for things that have happened here.
sentences.zh: 让我们为这里发生的事情承担一些后果吧。

sentences.en: Or whether Biden was trying to go back to a time that no longer existed.
sentences.zh: 或者拜登是否试图回到一个不再存在的时代。

sentences.en: You know, Biden says that he'll be a president for you, that he'll listen to you, that he wants to bring people together.
sentences.zh: 你知道，拜登说他会成为你的总统，他会倾听你的心声，他想把人们团结在一起。

sentences.en: When you hear that, what do you think?
sentences.zh: 当你听到这些时，你是怎么想的？

sentences.en: I don't believe it.
sentences.zh: 我不相信。

sentences.en: I'm sorry.
sentences.zh: 抱歉。

sentences.en: Oh, yeah, let's all come together.
sentences.zh: 哦，是的，让我们团结起来吧。

sentences.en: You have not earned it.
sentences.zh: 你还没赢得这种信任。

sentences.en: I pledge to be a president who seeks not to divide, but unify.
sentences.zh: 我承诺成为一位不寻求分裂，而是寻求团结的总统。

sentences.en: Who doesn't see red states and blue states, only sees the United States.
sentences.zh: 一个不分红州和蓝州，只看到美利坚合众国的人。

sentences.en: Still, when Biden won the White House.
sentences.zh: 尽管如此，当拜登赢得白宫时。

sentences.en: I sought this office to restore the soul of America.
sentences.zh: 我寻求这个职位是为了恢复美国的灵魂。

sentences.en: He doubled down on that promise.
sentences.zh: 他重申了这一承诺。

sentences.en: And now, the work of making that vision is real.
sentences.zh: 现在，实现这一愿景的工作是真实的。

sentences.en: It's a task, the task of our time.
sentences.zh: 这是一项任务，是我们这个时代的任务。

sentences.en: But let's be honest here.
sentences.zh: 但让我们诚实一点。

sentences.en: Took over the Capitol.
sentences.zh: 占领了国会大厦。

sentences.en: Overran the Capitol.
sentences.zh: 冲进了国会大厦。

sentences.en: We're in the fucking Capitol.
sentences.zh: 我们就在该死的国会大厦里。

sentences.en: We're in the fucking trailers.
sentences.zh: 我们就在该死的拖车里。

sentences.en: Drag them out by the fucking house.
sentences.zh: 把他们从该死的房子里拖出来。

sentences.en: He has the right to tell me what is best for this child.
sentences.zh: 他有权告诉我什么对这个孩子最好。

sentences.en: This is my child.
sentences.zh: 这是我的孩子。

sentences.en: Put your mask on.
sentences.zh: 戴上你的口罩。

sentences.en: Masking children is child abuse.
sentences.zh: 给孩子戴口罩是虐待儿童。

sentences.en: 65% of Americans say they are concerned about how things are going in the U.S.
sentences.zh: 65%的美国人表示他们担心美国目前的情况。

sentences.en: The soul of the nation is far from restored.
sentences.zh: 国家的灵魂远未恢复。

sentences.en: 72% of respondents believe America is headed in the wrong direction.
sentences.zh: 72%的受访者认为美国正朝着错误的方向前进。

sentences.en: They have the devil in them, and they're all going to burn in hell one day.
sentences.zh: 他们内心有魔鬼，总有一天他们都会在地狱里燃烧。

sentences.en: What kind of ridiculous is it what I got?
sentences.zh: 我这算是什么荒唐事？

sentences.en: Between a shooter and our kids.
sentences.zh: 在枪手和我们的孩子之间。

sentences.en: We didn't sign up for this shit.
sentences.zh: 我们可没报名参加这种烂事。

sentences.en: 85% of Americans say they are dissatisfied with how things are going, regardless of political party.
sentences.zh: 85%的美国人表示他们对现状感到不满，无论属于哪个政党。

sentences.en: Hello, is this Bishop Myers?
sentences.zh: 你好，是迈尔斯主教吗？

sentences.en: This is a Sted Herner from the New York Times.
sentences.zh: 我是《纽约时报》的阿斯特德·赫恩登。

sentences.en: Hello, how are you?
sentences.zh: 你好，你好吗？

sentences.en: I'm doing well.
sentences.zh: 我很好。

sentences.en: How are you?
sentences.zh: 你呢？

sentences.en: I'm well, thank you.
sentences.zh: 我很好，谢谢。

sentences.en: Good to hear your voice.
sentences.zh: 很高兴听到你的声音。

sentences.en: It's good to hear you, too.
sentences.zh: 我也很高兴听到你的声音。

sentences.en: It's been a couple of years.
sentences.zh: 已经过去几年了。

sentences.en: Yes, it has, man.
sentences.zh: 是的，伙计，确实是。

sentences.en: Now, in the run-up to this year's election, what's been the biggest change in the way that you view politics, if any, from two years ago to now?
sentences.zh: 现在，在今年选举的筹备阶段，与两年前相比，你对政治的看法最大的变化是什么（如果有的话）？

sentences.en: I guess the one thing that has bothered me is a very disheartening.
sentences.zh: 我想有一件事让我感到非常沮丧。

sentences.en: I've really lost faith in a lot of the political issues.
sentences.zh: 我真的对很多政治议题失去了信心。

sentences.en: Ah, I've lost faith in the people.
sentences.zh: 啊，我对人失去了信心。

sentences.en: What I'm finding when I talk to people all across the country...
sentences.zh: 当我和全国各地的人交谈时，我发现……

sentences.en: Feeling homeless in politics is, you know, it seems like there isn't a place for anybody to be.
sentences.zh: 在政治上感到无家可归，你知道，似乎没有任何地方适合任何人。

sentences.en: I know...
sentences.zh: 我知道……

sentences.en: ...is that there is a new level of political disconnect.
sentences.zh: ……是一种新的政治脱节感。

sentences.en: Political homelessness.
sentences.zh: 政治上的无家可归。

sentences.en: That's exactly how I feel.
sentences.zh: 我就是这种感觉。

sentences.en: A lot of people feel like everything is getting too extreme.
sentences.zh: 很多人觉得一切都变得太极端了。

sentences.en: You know, it's like the land of no more moderate.
sentences.zh: 你知道，就像是一个不再有温和派的土地。

sentences.en: And that this time, it extends well beyond political parties.
sentences.zh: 而且这一次，它远远超出了政党的范畴。

sentences.en: I definitely do not think the election was stolen.
sentences.zh: 我绝对不认为选举是被窃取的。

sentences.en: But I understand why the writers on January 6th were upset.
sentences.zh: 但我理解为什么1月6日的骚乱者会感到愤怒。

sentences.en: Beyond even Joe Biden and Donald Trump.
sentences.zh: 甚至超越了乔·拜登和唐纳德·特朗普。

sentences.en: I can't understand the frustration and the helplessness they feel and the need to revolt just because the system's not working for them.
sentences.zh: 我能理解他们感到的挫败感和无助感，以及仅仅因为体制对他们不起作用而产生的反抗需求。

sentences.en: It's about the political system as a whole.
sentences.zh: 这是关于整个政治体制的问题。

sentences.en: The voting system is not secure, and I'm just having doubts as to whether or not it'll make a difference if I vote at all.
sentences.zh: 投票系统不安全，我只是怀疑我投票到底会不会有任何改变。

sentences.en: People don't just feel divided.
sentences.zh: 人们不仅仅感到分裂。

sentences.en: I have very little hope for the future of the country.
sentences.zh: 我对国家的未来几乎不抱希望。

sentences.en: There's a deep sense of anxiety.
sentences.zh: 有一种深深的焦虑感。

sentences.en: There's nothing in this country here that really gives me hope.
sentences.zh: 这个国家没有任何东西能真正给我希望。

sentences.en: You know, it's really hard to have hope in politics when the news is so bad.
sentences.zh: 你知道，当新闻如此糟糕时，在政治上抱有希望真的很难。

sentences.en: This country just, it makes me sick, and I wish I could go to another country, but you can't.
sentences.zh: 这个国家，它让我感到恶心，我希望我能去另一个国家，但你做不到。

sentences.en: And the thing is, there's a reason people feel this way.
sentences.zh: 问题是，人们有理由这样感觉。

sentences.en: It has been a relentlessly disorienting time.
sentences.zh: 这是一个令人极其困惑的时代。

sentences.en: With demographic shifts that are increasingly changing the country's makeup.
sentences.zh: 人口结构的变化正在日益改变国家的构成。

sentences.en: Social movements that have changed cultural norms almost overnight.
sentences.zh: 几乎在一夜之间改变了文化规范的社会运动。

sentences.en: The explosion of new technology and misinformation that's amplified our divisions.
sentences.zh: 新技术和错误信息的爆炸式增长加剧了我们的分歧。

sentences.en: Add to that a global pandemic.
sentences.zh: 再加上全球大流行。

sentences.en: Widespread inequality.
sentences.zh: 普遍存在的不平等。

sentences.en: And rampant inflation.
sentences.zh: 以及猖獗的通货膨胀。

sentences.en: And through all of this, the political system has struggled to keep up.
sentences.zh: 在这一切之中，政治体制一直在努力跟上步伐。

sentences.en: To the point where we now have a Congress that's drifting further apart on the most urgent issues.
sentences.zh: 以至于我们现在的国会在最紧迫的问题上分歧越来越大。

sentences.en: Very few swing districts even up for grabs because of how election maps have been redrawn.
sentences.zh: 由于选举地图的重新划分，几乎没有什么摇摆选区可供争夺。

sentences.en: State houses that have become far more extreme than public opinion on issues like abortion and guns.
sentences.zh: 州议会在堕胎和枪支等问题上变得比公众舆论极端得多。

sentences.en: I think the state of democracy right now is very shaky.
sentences.zh: 我认为目前民主的状态非常不稳。

sentences.en: And so much change happening in the Supreme Court outside of voters' control.
sentences.zh: 最高法院发生了太多选民无法控制的变化。

sentences.en: I'm worried that democracy is being eroded.
sentences.zh: 我担心民主正在受到侵蚀。

sentences.en: Our democratic system is under direct threat.
sentences.zh: 我们的民主制度正受到直接威胁。

sentences.en: By nationalists and authoritarian groups.
sentences.zh: 来自民族主义者和威权主义团体。

sentences.en: I think democracy, I think it's much more fragile than I realize.
sentences.zh: 我认为民主，我觉得它比我意识到的要脆弱得多。

sentences.en: So I can see why some people feel like, what's the point of an election?
sentences.zh: 所以我能理解为什么有些人觉得，选举还有什么意义呢？

sentences.en: When the entire democratic experiment just might crumble.
sentences.zh: 当整个民主实验可能随时崩溃时。

sentences.en: Biden was elected.
sentences.zh: 拜登当选了。

sentences.en: If it hasn't already.
sentences.zh: 如果还没崩溃的话。

sentences.en: Poor man.
sentences.zh: 可怜的人。

sentences.en: He's just, he was not elected.
sentences.zh: 他只是，他根本没当选。

sentences.en: This is wrong.
sentences.zh: 这是错误的。

sentences.en: I feel like I'm living in a banana republic.
sentences.zh: 我觉得我生活在一个香蕉共和国。

sentences.en: If you could look ahead kind of to politics and where you think the country is headed, the direction of the country, what do you think your guess is?
sentences.zh: 如果让你展望一下政治前景，你觉得国家正走向何方，你对国家的发展方向有什么预判？

sentences.en: We're headed for destruction.
sentences.zh: 我们正走向毁灭。

sentences.en: I mean, whatever this country is supposed to mean, it never represented.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，无论这个国家原本意味着什么，它从未真正体现过。

sentences.en: It don't represent this country.
sentences.zh: 它代表不了这个国家。

sentences.en: It doesn't care about the people.
sentences.zh: 它根本不在乎人民。

sentences.en: But here's what I think.
sentences.zh: 但我的看法是这样的。

sentences.en: All these things that are making people feel so disconnected, they actually make the midterms more important than ever.
sentences.zh: 所有这些让人们感到如此疏离的事情，实际上让中期选举变得比以往任何时候都更加重要。

sentences.en: We are just 76 days away from the midterm elections that will determine which party controls Congress next year.
sentences.zh: 距离决定明年哪个党派控制国会的中期选举，我们只剩下76天了。

sentences.en: Because if Republicans take back the House.
sentences.zh: 因为如果共和党夺回众议院。

sentences.en: I have introduced articles of impeachment to impeach Joe Biden, impeach Kamala Harris.
sentences.zh: 我已经提交了弹劾乔·拜登和卡玛拉·哈里斯的弹劾条款。

sentences.en: Political divisions in Washington will only escalate.
sentences.zh: 华盛顿的政治分歧只会进一步加剧。

sentences.en: And I'll say this.
sentences.zh: 而且我要说的是。

sentences.en: If there's a prosecution of Donald Trump for mishandling classified information, there'll be riots in the streets.
sentences.zh: 如果唐纳德·特朗普因不当处理机密信息而受到起诉，街头将会发生骚乱。

sentences.en: And with the Supreme Court sending issues back to the states, the 2022 fall election will now be a referendum on abortion rights.
sentences.zh: 随着最高法院将相关议题交还给各州处理，2022年的秋季选举现在将成为一场关于堕胎权的公投。

sentences.en: Candidates who ran on the false claim that the 2020 election was stolen won primaries up and down the ballot.
sentences.zh: 那些宣扬“2020年大选被窃取”这一虚假主张的候选人，在各地的初选中纷纷获胜。

sentences.en: Huge decisions about abortion and voting rights are quite literally on the ballot.
sentences.zh: 关于堕胎和投票权的重大决定，实际上就摆在选票上。

sentences.en: Denying concerns and frustrations over the integrity of our local elections.
sentences.zh: 否认人们对地方选举公正性的担忧和挫败感。

sentences.en: Republicans have a slight two point edge when it comes to which party voters want to control Congress.
sentences.zh: 在选民希望哪个党派控制国会的问题上，共和党目前有微弱的两个百分点的优势。

sentences.en: A new polling shows a swing back toward Democratic candidates ahead of November's midterm elections.
sentences.zh: 最新的民调显示，在11月中期选举前，选民意向正向民主党候选人回流。

sentences.en: In places like Pennsylvania, Doug Mastriano, who did march to the Capitol on January 6th, is going to be the projected winner of that Republican primary for governor in Michigan.
sentences.zh: 在宾夕法尼亚州等地，曾于1月6日游行前往国会大厦的道格·马斯特里亚诺，预计将赢得密歇根州州长共和党初选。

sentences.en: This is going to be an epic battle between a conservative businesswoman and mother and a far left birthing parent and career politician.
sentences.zh: 这将是一场保守派女商人和母亲，与极左翼生育者及职业政客之间的史诗级对决。

sentences.en: In Arizona.
sentences.zh: 在亚利桑那州。

sentences.en: When I'm governor, we're going to take a sledgehammer to these damn electronic unions.
sentences.zh: 当我当选州长后，我们要用大锤砸碎这些该死的电子工会。

sentences.en: And finally, this is the first big test after January 6th and the Trump presidency of where Americans want the country to go.
sentences.zh: 最后，这是1月6日事件和特朗普总统任期结束后，美国人对国家未来走向的第一次重大考验。

sentences.en: 75% of Democrats saying they want someone besides President Biden to be the Democratic nominee in 2024.
sentences.zh: 75%的民主党人表示，他们希望2024年能有拜登总统以外的人选作为民主党提名人。

sentences.en: And who they trust to lead them there.
sentences.zh: 以及他们信任谁能带领他们走向未来。

sentences.en: And former President Donald Trump, still the most favored person for a potential 2024 presidential election.
sentences.zh: 而前总统唐纳德·特朗普，依然是2024年潜在总统大选中最受青睐的人选。

sentences.en: Florida Governor Ron DeSantis continues to raise his profile as the possible GOP frontrunner for 2024.
sentences.zh: 佛罗里达州州长罗恩·德桑蒂斯作为2024年共和党领跑者的可能性，其知名度持续上升。

sentences.en: So what I'm trying to figure out when I'm talking to voters, political power players.
sentences.zh: 所以，当我和选民、政治权力玩家交谈时，我试图弄清楚的是。

sentences.en: Another Clyburn.
sentences.zh: 另一位克莱伯恩。

sentences.en: Hi, Congressman Clyburn.
sentences.zh: 你好，克莱伯恩众议员。

sentences.en: Thank you so much.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢。

sentences.en: Kellyanne Conley.
sentences.zh: 凯莉安·康利。

sentences.en: Thank you so much for your time.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢你抽出时间。

sentences.en: Well, I gave you a lot of it.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我已经给了你很多时间了。

sentences.en: Try not to be too snarky and barky.
sentences.zh: 尽量别太尖酸刻薄。

sentences.en: And my colleagues at the Times.
sentences.zh: 还有我在《时报》的同事们。

sentences.en: I'm Maggie Haberman, and I cover politics.
sentences.zh: 我是玛吉·哈伯曼，我负责报道政治新闻。

sentences.en: I'm Lisa Lair, and I cover campaigns, elections.
sentences.zh: 我是丽莎·莱尔，我负责报道竞选和选举。

sentences.en: I'm Shane Goldmacher, and I'm a national political correspondent.
sentences.zh: 我是谢恩·戈德马赫，我是国家政治记者。

sentences.en: I'm Jenny Medina, and I'm a national politics reporter.
sentences.zh: 我是珍妮·梅迪纳，我是一名国家政治记者。

sentences.en: I'm Reid Epstein, and I cover campaigns and elections.
sentences.zh: 我是里德·爱泼斯坦，我负责报道竞选和选举。

sentences.en: I'm Maya King, and I cover Southeast politics.
sentences.zh: 我是玛雅·金，我负责报道东南部政治。

sentences.en: I'm Adam McGurney, and I have been covering national politics on and off since 1988.
sentences.zh: 我是亚当·麦格尼，自1988年以来，我一直断断续续地报道国家政治。

sentences.en: I want to get to more than just who's going to win in November.
sentences.zh: 我不仅想探讨谁会在11月获胜。

sentences.en: I want to ask some uncomfortable questions.
sentences.zh: 我还想问一些令人不适的问题。

sentences.en: Like, how did we get here?
sentences.zh: 比如，我们是怎么走到这一步的？

sentences.en: How deep do these fractures go?
sentences.zh: 这些裂痕有多深？

sentences.en: And in the end, how strong is our commitment to democracy really?
sentences.zh: 最后，我们对民主的承诺到底有多坚定？

sentences.en: From The New York Times, I'm Ested Herndon.
sentences.zh: 我是来自《纽约时报》的埃斯特德·赫恩登。

sentences.en: Welcome to The Run-Up.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听《The Run-Up》。

sentences.en: The New York Times app?
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》应用程序？

sentences.en: Unlocked?
sentences.zh: 解锁了？

sentences.zh: 大家都知道，你需要订阅《时报》才能获取所有报道。

sentences.en: But what if you could explore The Times for a month, for free, without putting in a credit card?
sentences.zh: 但如果能免费试用《时报》一个月，且无需绑定信用卡呢？

sentences.en: Now you can.
sentences.zh: 现在你可以了。

sentences.en: When you download The New York Times app for the first time, your first month in the app is free.
sentences.zh: 首次下载《纽约时报》应用程序，即可免费使用第一个月。

sentences.en: A month to go behind the paywall to see what Times subscribers get every single day.
sentences.zh: 用一个月的时间突破付费墙，看看《时报》订阅者每天都能获得什么。

sentences.en: If you don't already subscribe to The New York Times, download The Times app today and get free access for 30 days.
sentences.zh: 如果你还没有订阅《纽约时报》，今天就下载《时报》应用程序，获取30天的免费访问权限。

sentences.en: The Run-Up is reported by me, Ested Herndon, and produced by Elisa Gutierrez and Caitlin O'Keefe.
sentences.zh: 《The Run-Up》由我埃斯特德·赫恩登报道，由埃莉萨·古铁雷斯和凯特琳·奥基夫制作。

sentences.en: It's edited by Franny Car-Toth, Larissa Anderson, and Lisa Tobin.
sentences.zh: 由弗兰妮·卡-托斯、拉里萨·安德森和丽莎·托宾编辑。

sentences.en: With original music by Dan Powell, Marion Lozano, and Alishiba Itouk.
sentences.zh: 原创音乐由丹·鲍威尔、马里昂·洛萨诺和阿利希巴·伊图克创作。

sentences.en: It was mixed by Corey Shreppel and fact-checked by Caitlin Love.
sentences.zh: 由科里·施雷佩尔混音，凯特琳·洛夫进行事实核查。

sentences.en: Special thanks to Paula Schumann, Sam Dolnik, Julia Simon, Mahima Chablani, Shannon Busta, Nell Gologli, Jeffrey Miranda, Maddie Maciello, and Sydney Harper.

sentences.zh: 非常感谢大家的收听。

sentences.zh: 几十年来，布鲁克林民主党一直像一台严密控制的机器一样运作。

sentences.en: Until this summer.
sentences.zh: 直到今年夏天。

sentences.zh: 当选举迎来了一群自称改革者的人时。

sentences.en: Ever since, the party has been in the grip of a bruising, chaotic, and sometimes thrilling fight.
sentences.zh: 从那以后，该党一直陷入一场激烈、混乱，有时又令人兴奋的斗争中。
